articles.title: The Brazilian victory: left unity and digital autonomy
articles.author: Rezgar Akrawi
articles.content_excerpt: The leftist leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic victory in Brazil’s presidential election on October 25, 2026. The result came amid intense political and social polarization and the growing influence of the far right in Brazil and across Latin America, backed by the US far right led by Donald Trump. The significance of this electoral victory extends beyond Lula securing a fourth term. It also lies in the political and organizational experience that helped make it possible, above all the ability of diverse left-wing and progressive forces, with different programs and ideological outlooks, to forge a broad electoral alliance around common ground in confronting the far right. The US-drafted text, reportedly circulated among Security Council members on October 22, has drawn strong objections from the Polisario Front, the Sahrawi independence movement, as well as human rights and solidarity organizations. articles.title: One year after the election killings, Tanzania still awaits justice
articles.author: Nicholas Mwangi
articles.content_excerpt: One year ago, Tanzanians went to the polls in an election followed by deadly protests and a violent security crackdown. The immediate unrest has since subsided, but the wounds remain, and the demand for justice continues. President Samia Suluhu Hassan was declared the winner with 97.66% of the vote, an overwhelming margin that came with the exclusion of opposition forces and mounting restrictions on political activities. The disputed election and the violence that followed exposed deep tensions over Tanzania’s political realities, democratic participation, and the state’s response to dissent. A year on, not a single official has been held responsible, and justice for the victims and their families remains out of reach. articles.title: Dolores Huerta, Legendary Farmworker Organizer & Activist, Dies at 96
articles.content_excerpt: This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form. AMY GOODMAN : This is Democracy Now! , democracynow.org, The War and Peace Report . I’m Amy Goodman. The legendary labor organizer, feminist and civil rights activist Dolores Huerta has died at the age of 96. She was co-founder of the National Farm Workers Association in 1962 and then the United Farm Workers of America. She worked with Cesar Chavez at both groups. The United Farm Workers grew out of a merger between the National Farm Workers Association and the Filipino-led Agricultural Workers Organizing Committee. articles.title: Lula wins, Bolsonaro flees: What’s next for Brazil?
articles.author: Zoe Alexandra
articles.content_excerpt: Lula’s comeback to victory in Brazil’s 2026 presidential election was no accident. articles.title: The world once again calls for an end to the US blockade on Cuba
articles.author: Pablo Meriguet
articles.content_excerpt: Last Wednesday, October 28, the United Nations General Assembly voted (for the thirty-fourth time) in favor of ending the economic and commercial embargo – which many refer to as a blockade – that the United States has unilaterally imposed on Cuba for more than sixty years. With 130 votes in favor, 17 against, and 25 abstentions, the international community once again demanded that the United States end an embargo that has caused unimaginable hardship for the Cuban people and has slowed the Caribbean nation’s development. One of the countries that voted against the embargo was South Africa, whose ambassador emphasized his concern about the negative consequences the Cuban people are suffering as a result of Washington’s decisions.
